tools.name: verify_email
tools.description: Verify a single email address in real time with a live mailbox check. Returns status (deliverable, undeliverable, risky, unknown), a sub-status reason, a 0-100 quality score, and detailed checks (syntax, MX records, disposable, role-based, catch-all, typo detection). Costs 1 credit per call.

tools.name: find_email
tools.description: Find a person's business email address from their full name and company domain. Returns candidate addresses with confidence scores, based on published sources and common company address patterns. Finding is free, but candidates are pattern-based guesses until verified. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: verify_email, verify_bulk · Private data: verify_email, check_bulk_status, check_credits · Public sink: verify_email, find_email, verify_bulk.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: verify_email, verify_bulk · Private data: verify_email, check_bulk_status, check_credits · Public sink: verify_email, find_email, verify_bulk

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_bulk_status" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
